items.title: A descent datum gives a cosimplicial module, functorially
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a ring map R to A and a descent datum consisting of a module N together with an isomorphism, the lemma associates a cosimplicial module by the rules that its degree n part is the n-fold tensor construction and that a map of index categories acts by combining the descent isomorphism with the evident structure maps, and asserts functoriality in the datum (statement lines 590-602). The proof is a genuine verification: it first lists the low degree coface and codegeneracy maps explicitly, then checks the relation that the zeroth codegeneracy followed by the first coface is the identity, which is clear, and the relation with the second coface, which requires the cocycle condition: the composite is shown to be a projector by writing the descent isomorphism on elements and comparing with the cocycle identity, and since it is an isomorphism it must be the identity (proof lines 606-657). The remaining cosimplicial relations are then disposed of by noting that the relations among codegeneracies are obvious, those among cofaces come down to the cocycle condition, the mixed ones are checked in exactly the same way, and the others hold for any isomorphism whatsoever (proof lines 660-669). The claim is H2: the projector argument is the substance, and the remaining bookkeeping is stated with its reason.
